title: SkillEvo: Self-Renewing Evolution Gradients from Multi-Turn Interaction Feedback

analysis.tldr: SkillEvo argues that sustained procedural-memory evolution is limited by the feedback surface: multi-turn interaction keeps revealing new defects after earlier ones are repaired, while a separate governance layer prevents repeated edits from causing regression and bloat.
analysis.problem: Single-pass or single-turn skill evolution rapidly exhausts its feedback signal: once obvious gaps are patched, later defects that emerge only after several interaction turns remain invisible, and repeated editing can accumulate factual regression or structural bloat.
analysis.core_idea: Turn realistic multi-turn user simulation into the evolution signal generator, attribute exposed failures to skill defects, make bounded evidence-grounded revisions, and require an independent governor to inspect or repair degradation before each skill version is persisted.

memory_design.write: Start from hand-authored production Skills and revise skill/reference files only from attributed gaps that real tickets or faithful simulations expose; edits are evidence-bounded rather than free-form self-reflection.
memory_design.organize: Persistent procedural memory lives in SKILL.md plus reference files, with each evolution round retaining the intent, evidence, edit, inspection, and outcome for auditability.
memory_design.read: The updated skill remains the reusable knowledge/procedure consulted by the support agent during later multi-turn interactions; evaluation explicitly measures whether held-out tickets can be solved with the evolved artifact.
memory_design.update_forget: An outer evaluate→attribute→edit→evaluate loop runs up to four rounds. Independent governance checks factual regression and structural bloat, repairs or rejects degraded versions, and only inspected/evaluated checkpoints are persisted.

compared_to: single-turn-QA-driven evolution with attribution, revision, governance, and round count otherwise held fixed
analysis.evidence: On 9 production Tencent Cloud Skills and held-out real-ticket-derived evaluation sets, SkillEvo raises task success rate from 30.0% initially to 81.8% after four rounds. The clean feedback-source ablation is 81.8% for full SkillEvo versus 66.4% when multi-turn interaction is replaced by single-turn QA with attribution/revision/governance unchanged, supporting a 15.4-point contribution from the feedback modality. Removing governance gives 78.6%, a smaller -3.2 point change, while cumulative knowledge bloat rises from +2.8% with governance to +16.2% without it. The simulator reports 98.9% intent coverage and 95.3% human-rated fidelity on a 200-dialogue audit.
analysis.why_it_matters: For self-improving procedural memory, the scarce resource may be diagnostic feedback rather than editing capacity. The paper provides unusually clean evidence that a richer interaction failure surface can keep evolution useful after first-round defects are fixed, while governance serves a different role: preserving state quality rather than driving most of the score gain.
limitations: The evaluation is concentrated on cloud technical-support skills from one production domain and one organizational workflow.
Multi-turn feedback is generated by a simulator, so the result depends on simulator coverage/fidelity despite the authors' external audit.
The main comparison uses a representative single-turn-QA evolution baseline rather than reimplementing every recent skill-evolution method under the same multi-turn environment.
The skill artifact is explicit text/reference state; transfer to implicit policy updates or open-ended tool skills is not established.
